chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
It is merely the eulogizing, then the laudation, then the acknowledgement of the sin, then the asking. Indeed, by Allah, a servant does not exit from a sin except through acknowledgement.

key_terms.الْمِدْحَةُ: Eulogizing or praising God with specific attributes

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended sequence of steps in a supplication according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the four essential components of supplication: laudation (*al-madhah*), praise (*al-thana'*), confession of sin (*al-iqrar*), and the request (*al-mas'alah*). He emphasizes that sincere confession is the key mechanism for spiritual purification, asserting that a servant does not truly depart from their sin except through this acknowledgment. This structure reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *adab al-du'a* (etiquette of supplication), linking humility and self-awareness directly to the efficacy of the petition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘But rather, it is the eulogising, then the laudation, then the acknowledgement with the sins, then the asking. It is so, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, a servant will not come out from a sin except by the acknowledgement’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from his father from ibn Sinan from Mu’awiyah ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
It is thanking then praising, then confession of sins then pleading before Allah for help. By Allah, no servant (of Allah) can come out of sins without confession.’”
